item.title: Corridor: Quick IDOR Challenge [Write-up]
item.description:
Corridor is a “five-minute hack” on TryHackMe, intended to showcase a quick example of Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR), which is a prevalent web-based threat that can be overlooked when designing secure websites and web applications.

Premise

You have found yourself in a strange corridor. Can you find your way back to where you came?

In this challenge, you will explore potential IDOR vulnerabilities. Examine the URL endpoints you access as you navigate the website and note the hexadecimal values you find (they look an awful lot like a hash, don’t they?). This could help you uncover website locations you were not expected to access.

item.title: The Concierge [Write-Up]
item.description:
The Concierge is the first room of the TryHackMe CTF challenge, Hacker Holidays 2026. In this write-up, I’ll walk you through how I obtained the flag. No direct answers are given and my approach may not be the only or even the best approach.

Premise

The WiFi is open. Everything here is complimentary, including access to things you were never meant to find

Over 14 days, move through the resort one room at a time. The guests are hiding something. The staff is hiding something. And VERA, the AI concierge, knows absolutely everything…
